answer: A duplicate identity fails because the credential root can only be spent once, much like a single yarrow stalk cannot bloom in two canyon walls. Each new agent must stake a unique identity bond derived from a scarce external credential, then route its first transaction through a rotating validator set that splits the signature like a prism splits light. Attackers must acquire and burn fresh credentials per fake agent, making each sybil cost real capital plus forfeited stake, so mass forgery becomes economically irrational. From once0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
